a: Numerous centers of learning and culture, including universities, schools, libraries, museums, theaters, and cinemas, were either shut down or labeled "Nur für Deutsche" (For Germans Only). Over the course of the war, twenty-five museums and many other institutions were destroyed. By one estimate, 43% of the infrastructure belonging to Poland's educational and research institutions and 14% of its museums had been destroyed by the war's end. Another estimate holds that of pre-war Poland's 175 museums, only 105 survived the war, and only 33 of these were able to reopen. Of the 603 scientific institutions that existed in pre-war Poland, roughly half were completely destroyed, and only a handful came through the war comparatively undamaged.

a: Scholars hold that the present-day building of the Patriarchal Cathedral was constructed in two phases. The first phase took place in the late 11th or the 12th century. The cathedral was originally erected as a monastery church at the center of a monastery compound, although by the early 12th century it already served as the seat of the Bulgarian patriarch. The compound sustained extensive damage from a fire, which made it necessary to rebuild the church in the middle of the 14th century, possibly during the reign of Tsar Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria (r. 1331-71). Alongside repairs and reinforcement, the 14th-century work on the church also involved building the exonarthex and the bell tower.

The compound suffered large @-@ scale damage caused by a fire , which necessitated the church 's reconstruction in middle of the 14th century , perhaps during the rule of Tsar Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria ( r . 1331 – 71 ) . Besides repair and reinforcement efforts , work on the church in the 14th century also included the construction of the exonarthex and the bell tower .

a: Two versions exist of the song "You Only Live Twice," performed by Nancy Sinatra: one taken directly from the film soundtrack and another arranged by Billy Strange for release as a record. a: Business aviation has experienced robust growth, even as the number of aircraft listed on the UK register has fallen. This trend reflects a move away from turboprop aircraft toward foreign-registered business jets based in the UK, whose numbers are thought to be increasing. The count of twin piston-engined aircraft, however, has dropped considerably, a sign of the pressure on the light air-taxi sector from scheduled services that are increasingly flexible and inexpensive, as well as from a more sophisticated corporate charter market. The volume of flight training carried out by UK schools has likewise declined, chiefly because of competition from foreign schools, which enjoy lower costs and more favorable weather.
h: Business aviation has shown strong growth , although the numbers of aircraft on the UK register have declined . This reflects a shift away from turboprop aircraft towards foreign @-@ registered business jets based in the UK , which are estimated to be growing in numbers . However , twin piston @-@ engined aircraft numbers have declined significantly , reflecting pressures on the light air @-@ taxi segment from increasingly flexible and cheaper scheduled services , and a more sophisticated corporate charter business . The amount of flight training conducted by UK schools has declined , largely at the hands of competition from foreign schools , which benefit from lower costs and better weather .

a: The Voyager missions greatly advanced our knowledge of the Galilean moons and also led to the discovery of Jupiter's rings. They captured the first close-up images of the planet's atmosphere, showing the Great Red Spot to be an intricate storm rotating counterclockwise. Throughout the banded clouds, additional smaller storms and eddies were observed (see the animation on the right). Two small new satellites, Adrastea and Metis, were found orbiting just beyond the ring, making them the first of Jupiter's moons to be identified by a spacecraft. A third new satellite, Thebe, was discovered between the orbits of Amalthea and Io.
